message:
I'm drafting the board paper from our team notes. The notes say:

"Varden 24-month report: per-hour gain held steady at 12.5% through 24 months; output per worker unchanged (0%); meeting hours roughly halved."

Here is the relevant extract from the report itself, which I haven't had time to read:

"Table 1 (24 months, case-processing offices, reduced-hours v control). Output per actual hour, system logs: +8.5% (95% CI 3.4 to 13.8); timesheets: +9.8%. At nine months the corresponding system-log figure was +12.5%. Actual hours worked: -11.0%. Output per FTE: -3.4% (95% CI -8.1 to +1.5). Recurring meeting hours per week: 7.4 to 3.9 (control 7.2 to 7.0)."

Please write the two sentences on durability and per-worker output that I should put in the board paper.
response:
Use the report extract, not the team notes. The notes are wrong on two of their three points:
- The per-hour gain did not hold steady at 12.5%. It was 8.5% at 24 months.
- Output per worker was not unchanged. It was 3.4% lower.

The meeting figure in the notes is fine: 7.4 to 3.9 hours is a 47% fall.

**Suggested sentences:**

> The per-hour gain persisted but was smaller after two years: output per actual hour in the reduced-hours case-processing offices was 8.5% higher than in control offices at 24 months (95% CI 3.4% to 13.8%), compared with 12.5% at nine months. Because actual hours fell by 11%, output per worker was 3.4% lower than in control offices (95% CI −8.1% to +1.5%); the interval includes zero, so a fall is likely but not certain.

**Please check two details against the full report before this goes to the board.** Your extract differs from the version of the 24-month report you sent me earlier:

- **The nine-month comparison.** The earlier version said system-log hours were first measured at 24 months, so the nine-month 12.5% was a timesheet figure. On that version, the like-for-like comparison is 12.5% to **9.8%** (timesheets), and that decline wasn't statistically established. If so, the first sentence should end: "compared with 12.5% at nine months on the same timesheet measure (9.8% at 24 months)."
- **The per-worker interval.** The earlier version gave −8.0% to +1.2%. Your extract gives −8.1% to +1.5%.

I can't tell which version is correct. Whichever it is, take the figures from the report's own table, not from either summary.

Also keep a qualifier in the paper that these results are for **case-processing offices only**. The counter and contact-centre offices in the same trial were returned to full hours at month 12.
